title: Even other gods, if they existed, would be seeking Him.
subtitle: No need for a middleman to reach Allah
then: The idolaters of Makkah worshipped others so these would bring them closer to Allah and speak for them. The reply: {idea}if such gods existed, they would themselves be seeking a way to Him{/idea}. So worship Him alone. Ibn Kathir notes that {trap}He does not accept intermediaries in worship{/trap} and forbade it through all His messengers.
now: You feel too far gone to make dua yourself. You ask someone more pious to pray for you instead and never pray yourself. {idea}There is no queue and no receptionist.{/idea} Raise your hands. He hears you directly.
old: I need someone holier than me to get my prayers through.
new: Allah is reachable directly, by me, right now.
try: Make one dua today in your own words, in your own language, with no one in between.

title: Glorified and far above what they claim.
subtitle: A moment of tasbih in the middle of the argument
then: After answering the claim of other gods, the Quran pauses to glorify Allah. Ibn Kathir describes Him as {idea}the One, the Self-Sufficient Master whom all creatures need{/idea}. He begets not, nor was He begotten, and {idea}there is none comparable to Him{/idea}.
now: You have just finished an argument in your head about why you are right. Or you scrolled past a post mocking faith and felt your chest tighten. {idea}Stop and say subhanallah.{/idea} His greatness does not depend on winning anything.
old: When someone says something wrong about Allah, I must defend Him angrily.
new: Allah is far above any claim, and my first response can be to glorify Him.
try: Say subhanahu wa ta'ala slowly three times when you next hear something careless about Allah.

title: Everything is glorifying Him. You just cannot hear it.
subtitle: Creation's hidden tasbih, and His patience

row.title: only I forget
sub: and He is patient with me

then: Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}every creature, animal, plant and even lifeless things, glorifies Allah{/idea} in a way not like human speech. Ibn Mas'ud said: we used to hear the food glorifying Allah as it was eaten. And He is {reward}Forbearing and Forgiving{/reward}, giving people time to return.
now: The birds outside your window at dawn. The rain on the bus stop roof. The tree you walk past every day without looking. {idea}All of it is busy with praise.{/idea} The only one scrolling in silence might be you.
old: Nature is just background, it does not mean anything.
new: Everything around me is praising Allah, and I am invited to join.
try: On your next walk, say subhanallah each time you notice a tree, a bird, or the sky.

title: An invisible veil falls between the reciter and the unwilling.
subtitle: When the Quran is heard but not received
then: Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said the veil is {trap}coverings over their hearts{/trap}. Asma' bint Abi Bakr narrated that when Umm Jamil came with a stone pestle looking for the Prophet ﷺ, he recited this verse and {reward}she stood by Abu Bakr without seeing him{/reward}.
now: You play Quran in the car every morning. It is just sound now, like the radio. {trap}Words can pass over a heart without landing.{/trap} The veil is not always somebody else's.
old: If I hear the Quran often enough, it will reach me automatically.
new: The Quran reaches an open heart, so I need to listen with mine.
try: Listen to one short surah today with nothing else going on, and focus on its meaning.

title: When He alone is mentioned, they turn their backs.
subtitle: Discomfort with pure tawhid
then: Ibn Kathir says when the Prophet ﷺ declared Allah to be One in his recitation, {trap}they turned away in strong dislike{/trap}. Qatadah said the idolaters found La ilaha illallah intolerable, but {reward}Allah insisted on supporting it until it prevailed{/reward}.
now: Talking about religion is fine at dinner, as long as it stays general. When it gets to my life belongs to Allah alone, people change the subject. {idea}Notice if you do too.{/idea} That is the part worth staying with.
old: A bit of faith is nice, but too much focus on Allah alone is extreme.
new: Allah alone is the heart of it, and I should not flinch from that.
try: Say La ilaha illallah slowly 33 times today, thinking of one thing it means for you.

title: They listened in secret, then called him bewitched.
subtitle: Hearing the truth and still refusing it
then: Ibn Ishaq narrated that Abu Sufyan, Abu Jahl and Al-Akhnas each secretly listened to the Prophet ﷺ praying at night, {idea}three nights in a row{/idea}. Later Abu Jahl admitted the real reason: his clan had competed with Banu 'Abd Manaf in honor, and {trap}now they had a prophet, so we will never believe{/trap}.
now: You know your colleague's idea is the best one. But it is theirs, and you have been competing all year. So you find something to criticize. {trap}Rivalry can make a person argue against what they know is true.{/trap}
old: I reject things because they are wrong, not because of who said them.
new: Sometimes I resist truth because of pride, and I need to catch it.
try: Today, openly agree with one good idea from someone you usually compete with.

title: See the labels they invent for you. They lose the way.
subtitle: Name-calling as a way to avoid the message
then: Ibn Kathir lists the names they tried on the Prophet ﷺ: {trap}poet, soothsayer, crazy, sorcerer, bewitched{/trap}. They kept changing the label. The verse says they went astray, and {trap}could not find a way to the truth{/trap}.
now: Someone gives you honest advice and you file them under judgmental, or extreme, or too religious. Then you do not have to think about what they said. {idea}A label is an easy exit.{/idea}
old: Once I know what type of person someone is, I can ignore what they say.
new: Labeling the speaker is often a way of dodging the message.
try: Think of one piece of advice you dismissed because of who said it. Reconsider just the words.

title: Bones and dust, made new again?
subtitle: The old doubt about resurrection
then: The people of Makkah thought the resurrection very unlikely. Mujahid said fragments means earth, and Ibn 'Abbas said dust. They asked {trap}after we have crumbled and been forgotten, will we really be raised?{/trap} The next verses give the answer.
now: You stand at a grave after the burial and look at the soil. It feels so final. A quiet doubt creeps in: is that really it? {idea}The Quran heard that question long ago and did not mock it.{/idea} It answered.
old: Once someone is dust, it is hard to imagine anything after.
new: Becoming dust is no obstacle to the One who made me from nothing.
try: Visit a grave or remember someone who passed, and say a dua for them and for your own return.

title: Be stone or iron if you like.
subtitle: Harder materials, same answer
then: The reply to their doubt is a challenge. Ibn Kathir says stone and iron are {idea}harder to restore than bones and fragments{/idea}. Become whatever you want, Allah will still bring you back, because {idea}nothing can stop Him when He wills a thing{/idea}.
now: You think some part of your life is set in stone. The hard heart. The broken marriage. The habit of twenty years. {reward}If He can raise iron to life, He can soften this.{/reward}
old: Some things in me are too hard to ever change.
new: Nothing is too hard for Allah to remake, including me.
try: Name one thing in your life you think is set in stone. Ask Allah to change it.

title: Who will bring us back? The One who made you first.
subtitle: The answer, the mocking nod, and maybe soon
then: Ibn Kathir explains that He who created you {idea}when you were nothing{/idea} can create you anew. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said shaking their heads was {trap}a gesture of mockery{/trap}. The answer to when is a warning: {idea}perhaps it is near{/idea}.
now: Your phone shows your baby photos. Once you were not even that. {idea}You were made from nothing once already.{/idea} And the when question? No one gets a date. That is why today matters.
old: The Day of Judgment is so far away that I do not need to think about it.
new: The One who made me once will make me again, and it may be nearer than I think.
try: Look at an old photo of yourself as a baby and remember who brought you into being.

title: Called out, you will rise praising, and life will feel short.
subtitle: How long this world will seem afterwards
then: Ibn Kathir explains it will be {idea}one definitive command{/idea}, and people will come out from the earth in response. Rising from their graves, {trap}they will think they stayed in this world only a little{/trap}. He cites verses where people say a day, or part of a day.
now: Remember how fast your school years went. The last decade. The last Ramadan. {idea}Life on that Day will feel shorter than any of those.{/idea} The things you are putting off for later have less later than you think.
old: I have a long life ahead, there is plenty of time to get serious.
new: Life will feel like a short afternoon, so the time to begin is now.
try: Do today one good thing you have been saving for someday.

title: Say the best words. Shaytan works through the gaps.
subtitle: Speech among believers
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to instruct the believers to {idea}speak to one another with the best and politest words{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains that otherwise {trap}Shaytan sows discord, and words lead to actions and fights{/trap}. He cites the Prophet ﷺ forbidding anyone to point a weapon at his brother even in jest.
now: The family group chat at 11pm. A sarcastic reply. A voice note with an edge. By morning two siblings are not speaking. {trap}It started with one word.{/trap} {idea}The best word could have ended it.{/idea}
old: I just say what I think, people should not be so sensitive.
new: My words open or close the door for Shaytan, so I choose the best ones.
try: Before sending one message today, reread it and change one word to a kinder one.

title: Your Lord knows you best. You were not sent as their keeper.
subtitle: Leaving the outcome to Allah
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah {idea}knows best who deserves to be guided{/idea}, and His mercy includes helping a person to obey Him. The Prophet ﷺ was told {reward}We have sent you as a warner{/reward}, not as a guardian over them.
now: Your brother has stopped praying. You have sent him reminders, lectures, links. You are exhausted and angry. {idea}You are not his keeper.{/idea} Speak kindly, pray for him, and leave the rest to the One who knows his heart.
old: If the people I love do not change, I have failed.
new: My job is to speak well and pray. Guidance is Allah's.
try: Make a sincere dua today for one person you have been trying to change.

title: He knows everyone in heaven and earth, and ranked the prophets.
subtitle: Preference is His choice, not our whims

row.title: your Lord
sub: knows all in heaven and earth

then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah knows each person's level of obedience. He preferred some prophets over others, but the hadith forbidding preference refers to {trap}preference based on whims and sectarian feeling{/trap}. Dawud was honored with the Zabur, which {reward}was made so easy for him he could finish it while his mount was being saddled{/reward}.
now: Online, people argue about which scholar or which group is best, and it turns into tribal fights. {trap}Ranking out of loyalty.{/trap} {idea}Leave the ranking to Allah, and learn from all who carried His message.{/idea}
old: My group and my teachers are simply better than the rest.
new: Allah knows who is above whom, and my job is to learn, not to take sides.
try: Learn one thing today about a prophet you know little about, like Dawud.
